Research directions, potential applications, and real-world use cases across the Lab’s two complementary pillars. These are ideas for investigation, not completed studies or announced projects.

title: Research
text:
Governance of AI
Understanding how AI systems should be assessed, governed, and held accountable.



RESEARCH IDEA · ILLUSTRATIVE


Accountability, safety, and oversight

Social Welfare Public Administration

How can institutions evaluate AI systems, identify risks, and remain accountable for AI-assisted decisions?

Real-world example

A government agency uses AI to help review applications for social assistance. What safeguards, explanations, and appeal mechanisms should protect people affected by its recommendations?






RESEARCH IDEA · ILLUSTRATIVE


Evidence and real-world impact

Healthcare

How can we distinguish claims of AI effectiveness from reliable evidence about its actual consequences?

Real-world example

A hospital introduces AI-assisted clinical decision support. Does it improve outcomes for patients, or only perform well on a test dataset? How could researchers assess the difference?

title: Research
text:
AI for Governance
Exploring the design and evaluation of AI systems that could improve institutional work, public policy, and human decision-making.



RESEARCH IDEA · ILLUSTRATIVE


Human-AI decision-making

Regulatory Oversight

How should people and AI systems work together when institutional decisions have important consequences?

Real-world example

A regulator uses an AI agent to flag cases for review. How should staff verify its recommendations, correct mistakes, and retain control over final decisions?






RESEARCH IDEA · ILLUSTRATIVE


AI tools for policy and regulatory work

Public Policy

What kinds of AI tools could help institutions analyze evidence, monitor developments, or improve public-sector processes?

Real-world example

A policy team needs to examine thousands of consultation submissions. Could an AI tool organize recurring themes and supporting evidence while keeping its findings traceable to the original documents?

title: Research
text:
Connecting Research and Implementation
A research question may lead to a policy analysis, an empirical evaluation, a prototype, or a collaboration with another institution. Some projects may involve Design → Develop → Evaluate; others may focus on one stage. Governance considerations and evidence quality matter throughout.
The Lab draws on AI, machine learning, statistics, econometrics, causal inference, economics, public policy, decision science, and software engineering. Methods should follow the questions being investigated.
Explore existing projects and prototypes →

All use cases are hypothetical examples, not commissioned work or existing deployments. Research topics and possible collaborations remain open to refinement.

title: Home
text:
Two Complementary Pillars
We explore both how AI should be governed and how AI can improve governance.



GOVERNANCE OF AI

How can we ensure AI systems are effective, safe, accountable, and beneficial?
Research, risk and impact assessment, evidence-based evaluation, and institutional oversight.



AI FOR GOVERNANCE

How can we design AI systems that improve institutional decisions and public services?
Human-AI decision support, applied AI systems, GovTech, RegTech, and policy tools.




ONE INTEGRATED APPROACH


Design → Develop → Evaluate
The two pillars can work together throughout a project’s lifecycle: from understanding institutional challenges and developing AI solutions to evaluating their real-world impact. Projects may cover the full lifecycle or focus on individual stages. Governance and empirical evidence inform the process from the beginning.





01


Design
Understand decisions, user needs, potential benefits, and risks.




02


Develop
Build and integrate AI-enabled tools with human oversight.




03


Evaluate
Examine effectiveness, fairness, uncertainty, and real-world impact.

title: About
text:
ABOUT



AI Governance Lab is an independent, early-stage research and technology initiative working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, human decision-making, governance, and public policy.
Its mission is to advance governance and public policy through the design, development, and rigorous evaluation of AI systems. The Lab aims to connect empirical research with practical technology, without separating the building of AI systems from examining their benefits, risks, and real-world effects.

title: About
text:
Research & Collaboration
The Lab is open to conversations about independent research, academic collaborations, and carefully scoped applied AI projects with public institutions, researchers, policy organizations, and organizations in regulated sectors.
